newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds Commission right to end to Air Inter deal.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds Commission right to end to Air Inter deal.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance confirmed on Thursday the European Commission had authority to end Air Inter's exclusive air transport arrangement within the French airport system.

The court confirmed that although Air Inter, as a direct beneficiary of an exlusive air transport arrangement within the French airport system, did have a right to defend its position, that right was respected by the Commission because it had an opportunity to be heard before the final decision was taken.

The court went so far as to say that because Air Inter did not put legal arguments directly before the Commission it created the impression that Air Inter believed the Commission was adequately informed by the French authorities on the legal issues at stake.

TAT European Airlines asked the Commission to adopt a decision under Council rules set up to ensure open competition in the air transport services sector and argued the French government was discriminating against transport providers by granting Air Inter an exclusive contract between Paris Orly airport and airports in Marseille and Toulouse.

The court found the Commission acted correctly when it ended the exclusive contract between France and Air Inter under article 8(3) of Council regulation 2408/92 on access to intra-Community air routes and said the Commission was not required to find France failed to meet member state obligations.
"Air transport - Regulation (EEC) No 2408/92 - Rights of the defence - Principle of good faith - Article 90(2) of the EC Treaty"
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, interveners
